conviction_note: Two measurements that roughly agree: the findings sum to +1.90, a positive company track record (EBITDA above the top of guide three quarters running, reactions +48/+11/+35 to beat-and-raise) plus memory ASP inflation, netted against a direct peer (Logitech, -12% on a beat) saying component cost and availability pressure has spread from memory to all electrical components and IDC calling Q4 PC units -20%. The scaled number is a near-coin-flip p_up 53 on a 16% absolute move, because the print turns on the Q4 guide and the guide is where the peer evidence cuts the other way.

positioning_check: Short interest: 10.9M shares at the 2026-08-14 settlement, 3.7 days to cover (Curved Trading, FINRA data, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/crsr/short-interest/), and 11.8M shares, 8.0 days, about 10.9% of float as of 2026-08-20 (https://equibles.com/stocks/crsr/shortinterest). Stock is down 7.72% over 5 days and -3.21% over 20, 11.7% below its 52-week high and 177% above its low. The options market leans long into the print.

findings.finding: Logitech, the closest listed peer, reported 2026-10-27 that component shortages 'have expanded from just memory to basically all electrical components' and that this is industry-wide and hits the gross margin outlook. It guided its own Dec-quarter gross margin down about 200bp YoY on material and logistics costs plus more promotion, and LOGI fell more than 12% pre-market despite beating. Corsair's Aug 6 guide named only memory pricing as the pressure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CRSR's one guide cut in the baseline, Q3 2025 (2025-11-04, FY narrowed and lowered), moved -13.16%. Guide raises moved +48.25% (2026-02-12) and +35.25% (2026-08-06).
findings.why_not_priced: Corsair has said nothing since Aug 6, before the peer's statement, so its guide predates the spread of cost pressure beyond memory. CRSR is -7.7% over 5 days, which may be part of the read-through. But calls are still bid (skew -11.9, P/C OI 0.21), which does not look like a market positioned for a margin-led Q4 cut.
findings.independence: Same document as the Logitech demand finding below (one call, read on two lines). The press reaction is a separate source: https://finviz.com/news/410093/logitech-shares-fall-over-12-as-supply-chain-disruption-overshadows-q2-earnings-beat. Part of Logitech's issue is its own semiconductor supplier closure, which may not apply to Corsair.

findings.finding: On the same call Logitech reported gaming net sales +7% cc and Americas +13% in the Sept quarter, said holiday demand is expected to be positive (K-shaped, premium spending holding), and pointed to Call of Duty MW4. That supports Corsair's guide of low-double-digit growth in Gamer & Creator Peripherals (Q3 2025 base $112.7M). Logitech also said GTA 6 is console-first and is not a giant upside for a PC-centric business.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Corsair Peripherals +13% in Q2 2026 came with a +35.25% reaction, alongside the guide raise and tariff refund, so the move cannot be attributed to this line alone.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer print after Corsair last spoke. Logitech's growth (+7%) is below the rate Corsair guided for its peripherals, so it confirms the guide rather than beating it. That is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: Same Logitech document as the finding above; counts once in substance. Corsair's own Q2 peripherals +13%: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001743759/000119312526337943/crsr-ex99_1.htm

findings.finding: IDC put Q3 2026 worldwide PC shipments at -20.1% YoY (62.7M units), forecast Q4 at about -20%, and expects the memory shortage to last at least to end-2027 (Omdia: -21.2%). That pressures Corsair's Gaming Components & Systems (63% of Q2 revenue), which was already guided down low double digits YoY in H2 (Q3 2025 base $233.1M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Components fell 10% in Q1 2026 and 9% in Q2 2026, and the stock still moved +11.14% and +35.25%. This line has not driven the reaction while the company called it in advance.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The Q3 part sits inside the guide, which already said components down low double digits. What is not priced is a Q4 that IDC now calls -20% against Corsair's implied Q4 of about $431M, roughly flat YoY. This is OEM-unit data, a proxy for DIY demand, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Logitech cites the same -20% PC shipments figure (transcript above). Corsair itself: 'elevated memory pricing continues to delay DIY PC builds' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001743759/000119312526337943/crsr-ex99_1.htm).

findings.finding: Retail DDR5 prices kept climbing through Q3: 32GB DDR5 kits were about $350-480 in October 2026 against $100-200 a year earlier, and a French tracker showed DDR5-6400 medians +12.6% over 30 days to 2026-10-18. Corsair memory revenue was $117.2M in Q3 2025 and grew 17% YoY in Q2 2026 on ASP and North American share gains. If units hold, ASP inflation lifts Q3 revenue toward the top of the $320-350M guide, though memory gross margin is guided to moderate to the high teens in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Memory +6% in Q1 2026 (stock +11.14%) and +17% in Q2 2026 (+35.25%). Q3 2025 had memory $117.2M with a -13.16% reaction, but that move came on a lowered FY guide.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (page re-checked on the October 2026 snapshot; the year is in the title)
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus ($332-343M) sits at the guide midpoint, not the top, so the street has not credited the extra price inflation since August. Management flagged that ASPs 'may rise further toward year-end', so part of it is inside the guide. This is a retail price proxy, not company units, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Memory-segment economics from Corsair's own Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15398317698327552), and the French price tracker (https://www.comparateur-gamer.fr/evolution-prix/ram).

findings.finding: Corsair has beaten its own guide three quarters running. Q4 2025 adj. EBITDA was $53.6M, above the high end; Q1 2026 was $35.8M, above the high end, with revenue $354.5M above the midpoint; Q2 2026 was $16.6M ex-refund, above the high end, with revenue $314.3M above the midpoint. It raised the FY EBITDA midpoint by about $19M in August. The Q3 guide is $18-21M EBITDA on $320-350M revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat-and-raise prints moved +48.25% (2026-02-12), +11.14% (2026-05-07) and +35.25% (2026-08-06). The one guide cut (2025-11-04) moved -13.16%. This name pays for beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Consensus EPS of $0.12 is already at the top of the $0.09-0.12 guide, and the call-bid skew says the market expects upside. What is not priced is the size of a fourth consecutive beat on a thin float.

findings.finding: Corsair named GTA 6 (Nov 19, 2026) as a Q4 catalyst on its Aug call. No further delay was found. But GTA 6 launches on console only, with PC 'much later into next calendar year' per Logitech, so the catalyst is weaker for a PC-centric peripherals maker than Corsair's framing suggested.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The release date has been public since Nov 2025. What may be new is that the Q4 guide includes some GTA-driven demand, though how much is unquantified. Sized near zero.
findings.independence: Logitech transcript (above) on console-first. Release date: https://www.pcgamesn.com/grand-theft-auto-vi/gta-6-delayed-november-2026

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly positive, which agrees with the call-bid skew (-11.9) and the beat-paying reaction history. The peer evidence on Q4 costs and PC units cuts against both, and the -7.7% five-day drift may be the market already taking some of that in, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7: both peer/IDC negatives run against a -11.9 call-bid skew and roughly 11M shares short on a small float, so they were shrunk: Logitech cost -1.5 to -1.0, IDC -1.0 to -0.6.

Lesson 5/6: IDC's Q3 shipments sit inside Corsair's guide (components down low double digits) and are OEM-unit data, a proxy, so it stays small. The memory-ASP proxy went +1.5 to +1.0 because management had already flagged rising ASPs.
Lesson 6 (exit window): the EagleTree resale-shelf overhang (-0.5) moved to outside_window, since a secondary would typically launch after the first full session.

Lesson 1/8: the reaction history pays beat-and-raise (+48, +35, +11), so the beat-track-record finding stays at +1.5 and abs_move stays at 16, above the 15.76 implied move, because a Q4 guide comes with the release.
p_up moved 52 to 53 after the negatives were shrunk. The draft sum of +1.0 became a final sum of +1.9.
